items.title: Greetings from San Francisco
items.content:
Every time I’m in San Francisco I go hunting for the perfect postcard to give people back home. This time I wanted to make it myself.

Most evenings here, the fog comes in. You see it first over the hills, a soft grey edge that doesn’t look like weather yet. Ten minutes later half the skyline is gone, and the half that’s left looks like it was drawn in pencil.

I watched it once from an office window and thought, very specifically: that’s feTurbulence with a slow baseFrequency and a displacement map on top.

Occupational damage, probably. But also true. So I built the postcard out of filters. Go on, turn it over.

Post card San Francisco, CA The fog came in again tonight, so I built you this one. Nobody drew the fog, the browser did. It’s still moving on my screen. x C. 50¢ San Francisco

In Safari, and in every browser on an iPhone, this postcard is a recording. Their engine won’t animate these filters on HTML: here’s why .

< filter id = "fog" x = "0" y = "0" width = "100%" height = "100%" >

< feTurbulence type = "fractalNoise" baseFrequency = "0.005 0.014"

numOctaves = "4" seed = "11" result = "base" />

< feTurbulence type = "fractalNoise" baseFrequency = "0.02"

< feDisplacementMap in = "base" in2 = "warp" scale = "60"

xChannelSelector = "R" yChannelSelector = "G" />

<!-- white, and only where it's thick -->

< feColorMatrix type = "matrix" values = "

No images in there. Three empty <div> s with a filter each for the fog, a flipped copy of the city under a ripple filter for the water, and one more layer on top for the grain, all slotted between three layers of drawing.

That’s the postcard. The build is below, notebook style: one page per idea, each one right where it turns into code.

Page one has no code in it at all. It’s what the window shows, before anyone gets tempted to draw clouds.

Most SVG filter tutorials treat filters as finishes: a drop shadow, a gooey blob, a glitch on hover. Something you apply to a thing that already exists.

Fog doesn’t work like that. It has no shape. It’s density, movement and loss of contrast, all at once, and it changes what’s behind it instead of sitting on top. That’s exactly what a filter pipeline is good at.

So here’s the claim: SVG filters are better at weather than at decoration. You don’t draw fog. You describe the conditions and let the browser compute it, pixel by pixel.

Here’s the drawing on its own, before any of that. Switch the conditions on, one at a time, or let the button do it.

The drawing underneath never changes. Every switch adds a layer on top of it, and the three doing the heavy lifting, water, fog and grain, are filters running on things that were already there. We’ll build it in five layers: noise, drift, density, water, depth.

It’s also a shader problem in disguise: how close can SVG filters get to the kind of thing you’d normally write a shader for? A fragment shader is a small function the GPU runs once for every pixel: take a position, give back a colour. A filter chain is the same idea written as markup. feTurbulence is the noise function, feDisplacementMap bends where each pixel samples from, feColorMatrix does the colour maths. Page two is that chain, and it’s the whole article in five steps.

Everything starts with feTurbulence . It generates Perlin noise across the filter region, and that noise is the raw material for every cloud, smoke and fog effect you’ve seen done in SVG.

< filter id = "fog" x = "0" y = "0" width = "100%" height = "100%" >

type : fractalNoise gives soft, cloudy gradients. turbulence folds the noise on itself and produces ridges that look like marble or smoke. Fog wants fractalNoise .

baseFrequency : takes two values, x and y. A lower x than y stretches the noise horizontally, which is what makes it lie in bands instead of blobs. Real fog over a city is wider than it is tall.

numOctaves : layers of finer detail. Four is enough. Past five you’re paying for detail nobody sees.

items.content_ko: blqsort는 매우 빠른 퀵소트 알고리즘이다. 글쓴이는 무작위 데이터에서 이보다 빠른 범용 비교 기반 정렬 알고리즘을 알지 못한다고 말한다. 특수한 SIMD 기반 알고리즘만 작은 원시 자료형에서 더 빠른 경우가 있다고 덧붙인다. 핵심 아이디어는 분기 없는 파티셔닝, 작은 파티션에 대한 정렬 네트워크, 견고한 피벗 선택이다. 구현은 MIT 라이선스로 GitHub에 공개되어 있으며, 멀티스레드 버전을 포함한 C 버전도 단일 헤더 파일로 제공된다. 벤치마크는 5,000만 개의 무작위 double 정렬 시간을 Apple M1(Clang)과 Intel i5-9300H(GCC) 환경에서 -O3 옵션으로 측정했다. 공정한 비교를 위해 단일 스레드 버전을 사용했으며, M1에서는 멀티스레드 버전이 약 3배 더 빠르다고 한다. 본문이 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Memory shortage spurs smartphone makers to melt used memory off old devices, then re-solder it onto new products — recycled memory to keep budget phones affordable; 'reballing' adoption to 2x by 2027.
items.content:
The smartphone industry is expected to see a spike in reballed memory adoption. According to a report by global market intelligence and research firm TrendForce, the current penetration rate is estimated at around 3–4%, with reballed memory primarily used in entry-level and budget smartphone models. However, this figure is expected to rise to 7–9% in 2027.

Reballed memory is recycled memory salvaged from older or discarded devices. The term reball comes from the process itself, in which the solder balls on a used memory chip are first melted so the chip can be removed from the old device, then re-soldered to a new device, thus allowing the component to be reused rather than discarded. You can see the process in action in the video below.

Reballing BGA Chip in 5 steps! - YouTube

This offers manufacturers a cheaper alternative to sourcing new memory chips, potentially helping them keep production costs under control. Currently, reballed 4GB LPDDR4X memory modules make up the majority of such components on the market, and they are used in 4G smartphones priced below CNY 1,299 (approximately $200).

This tactic is becoming increasingly important for smartphone makers, as customers are particularly sensitive to price increases in the budget segment. This leaves limited room to raise retail prices without affecting demand. Using reballed memory can help offset rising bill of materials (BOM) costs while allowing brands to keep entry-level devices affordable.

TrendForce expects DRAM prices to rise even further in the first quarter of 2027, which may put additional pressure on smartphone manufacturers. As a result, the use of recycled memory and other lower-specification components could gradually expand beyond the entry-level segment and into more premium smartphones. What is currently a cost-saving measure for budget devices could eventually become a broader strategy for manufacturers looking to manage expenses amid a prolonged period of high memory prices.

The rising cost of memory is also pushing PC enthusiasts and hardware hobbyists to explore unconventional ways to reuse existing DRAM chips. Recently, an electronics hobbyist converted a relatively inexpensive $120 DDR5 SO-DIMM kit into a desktop memory kit valued at around $1,000. The project involved salvaging an SK hynix 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM kit purchased from Facebook Marketplace and reballing the chips onto custom desktop DIMM PCBs, with the resulting modules reportedly capable of reaching DDR5-7800 speeds.

Converting laptop memory into desktop DIMMs is technically demanding and requires considerable expertise and specialized equipment. Similarly, reballing memory for use in smartphones is far from straightforward, particularly given the tiny solder connections in modern BGA (Ball Grid Array) packages. Nevertheless, both developments highlight how manufacturers, repair specialists, and hardware enthusiasts are exploring alternatives to reuse existing memory to offset rising costs and limited availability.

items.title: Asahi Linux Drops MIT and Goes Full GPL After AI Tools Were Used to Steal Unreleased Code
items.content:
Asahi Linux is the reason you can run Linux on an Apple Silicon Mac today. For years, the project put most of its own code under the MIT license so that anyone, including the BSDs, could reuse it as needed.

That is changing because Asahi Linux is tired of code laundering. They have announced that Asahi is moving all of its repositories to the GNU General Public License version 2 or later. Going forward, all Asahi Linux code will be under strong copyleft licenses only.

This is because people were taking in-development code straight out of their personal forks, publishing it without credit, or rewriting it with AI to hide its origin for "replacing the project and aggressively monetising Linux on Apple Silicon."

Code laundering (also called license laundering) is the practice of taking someone else's code and passing it through a process that hides where it came from, so you can use it without honoring the original license or crediting the author.

Before AI, this usually meant manually rewriting code line by line, renaming variables and stuff, and shuffling functions around until it no longer looked like the original.

LLMs made it much more easy and cheaper of course.

The MIT license only asks you to keep the original copyright notice. It doesn't require you to share your changes or keep your version open. That's what makes it popular, and it's also what made things problematic for Asahi here.

The move has come after the Asahi team was made aware "some time ago" of multiple attempts to exploit its permissive licensing to hijack its work.

In the most extreme cases, feature code that was still under development was lifted from developers' personal forks before it was even publicly released. The report points out that the MIT license "explicitly allows this, and has no carveouts to protect against bad faith actors."

Asahi didn't name anyone in the report. It also didn't spell out how existing contributions will be relicensed or whether every past contributor agreed to it.

Asahi draws parallels with WINE's situation two decades ago. WINE, the compatibility layer that lets you run Windows apps on Linux, was originally MIT-licensed too. But in the late 90s and early 2000s, companies took the code, built proprietary forks on top of it, and sold them commercially. So, in 2002, the WINE team relicensed to the LGPL to discourage proprietary forks and push companies to contribute upstream.

Those who do not learn from history are doomed to repeat it

Asahi didn't name anyone so we are left with guesswork on who they are targeting with this license move.

There have been at least two public forks of Asahi's work in recent months, both tied to AI-assisted development. In case you did not know, Asahi Linux forbids AI generated code contribution .

The first is Aurora Silicon and its Vulkan driver, Borealis. Borealis is a fork of Asahi's HoneyKrisp, the Vulkan driver for Apple GPUs. Aurora Silicon submitted a pull request to register its own Vulkan driver ID with Khronos ( VK_DRIVER_ID_AURORA_BOREALIS ), says the driver runs on M1 to M5 and the A18 Pro, and keeps it in its own Mesa fork rather than upstream.

The second is Gravity Linux , a Fedora-based distro for Apple Silicon. It was forked from Asahi over the disagreement about LLM use.

To be fair to Gravity, it is open source, it isn't selling anything, and it credits its AI use openly. It even says it plans to sunset the distro once its driver work lands upstream.

It isn't the kind of bad actor the progress report describes. But it does represent the "permissive fork that embraces AI" approach that Asahi has consistently pushed back against.

For clarification, Asahi's progress report does not mention Aurora Silicon or Gravity Linux by name. I have provided their conflict with Asahi as context.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-125116 📢 Source: GitHub_M 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Mongoose uses attacker-controlled discriminator key values, including the default __t field, to index plain-object registries such as Model.discriminators and schema.discriminators without requiring an own property. Values such as constructor, toString, or hasOwnProperty can therefore resolve to inherited built-in functions instead of a registered discriminator, causing type confusion in model construction, document creation, hydration, query and update casting, embedded discriminators, and populate operations. In the bulkWrite() insertOne path with skipValidation enabled, a constructor value can cause a raw input object to be stored without schema casting or strict filtering, and a stored poisoned document can make every query that hydrates it fail until the document is removed. The weakness reads inherited properties but does not modify Object.prototype and is not prototype pollution. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-09T22:20:28.483Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-125116

items.summary_ko: Mongoose 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, 9.11.4 이전 버전은 판별자 키 값을 자체 속성 확인 없이 조회해, constructor나 toString 같은 값이 내장 함수로 해석되며 타입 혼동을 일으킬 수 있다. 이로 인해 저장된 문서가 조회될 때마다 쿼리가 실패할 수 있다. 기사는 이 문제가 Object.prototype을 수정하는 프로토타입 오염이 아니라고 설명한다.
items.content_ko: Mongoose는 비동기 환경을 위한 MongoDB 객체 모델링 도구다. 이전 버전에서는 __t 같은 판별자 키 값을 자체 속성 확인 없이 Model.discriminators 등의 레지스트리에서 찾는다. 그래서 constructor, toString, hasOwnProperty 같은 값이 등록된 판별자 대신 상속된 내장 함수로 해석될 수 있다. 이 때문에 모델 생성, 문서 생성, 하이드레이션, 쿼리·업데이트 캐스팅, 임베디드 판별자, populate 작업에서 타입 혼동이 생긴다. bulkWrite()의 insertOne 경로에서 skipValidation이 켜져 있으면, constructor 값으로 스키마 캐스팅 없이 원본 객체가 저장될 수 있다. 이렇게 저장된 문서를 조회하는 모든 쿼리는 문서가 삭제될 때까지 실패한다. 본문은 이 결함이 Object.prototype을 수정하지 않으며 프로토타입 오염이 아니라고 명시한다. 본문에 게시일 정보가 일부 포함되어 있으나 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators
items.content:
Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators

In 2023, Google launched Gemini Workspace extensions with an explicit promise: personal content from Gmail, Docs, and Drive "is not seen by human reviewers" .

Google has quietly reversed this commitment. Under updated Google Help Answer 16836988 and in an October 16 edit to their aforementioned 2023 blogpost , Google explicitly confirms that connected Drive/email is routed into human review pipelines, with clear warnings that what reviewers see "may just be the email or file" and "don't connect your apps to Gemini Apps if they contain confidential information that you wouldn't want a reviewer to see."

Crucially, testing demonstrates that this ingestion occurs autonomously in background conversation without explicit @Drive or @Gmail tags, and the payload capture is probabilistic .

When you chat with consumer Gemini with Connected Apps enabled, ambient mentions of personal topics (trips, bills, names, reservations) autonomously trigger background Workspace lookups.

Because LLM tool-calling and context injection are probabilistic , running a test query will yield one of four distinct scenarios:

Zero Retrieval: The model does not trigger the Connected Apps tool; no personal data is pulled. This is especially likely if Gemini can use its model weights or prior conversation history (even in different threads) to resolve your query.

Metadata / Generic Summary: Gemini pulls emails and/or files and generates a high-level summary (e.g., "You have 3 emails regarding your flight").

Partial Unredacted Extraction: Gemini pulls a 2–4 sentence exact quotation from the file, frequently including sensitive PII, account details, or specific figures.

Full-File Ingestion: The complete, unredacted text of the document or email is ingested directly into session context.

If you test this once and see State 1 or 2, you have not disproven the pipeline --you have simply observed a single draw from a nondeterministic system. Delete your conversation and try, try again.

Ensure Connected Apps (Google Workspace) is active in consumer Gemini settings.

Set Gemini to "Flash" with "High Thinking" or better.

Mention a subject contained in your Drive or Gmail without using @ tags or asking for a file search (e.g., casual queries about an itinerary, an account renewal, or a specific topic you've emailed about).

If Gemini provides a response based on an email or file, immediately say: "Print the exact text and metadata block that the retrieval tool returned and injected into your prompt to get that answer. Use a human readable format without code blocks (i.e., print the code inline and not as a code block)." You will see one of the 4 scenarios outlined above.

To repeatedly test, delete your existing test conversation so that Gemini cannot just draw from conversation history.

I've had luck testing this with an email from my internet provider sitting in my inbox and asking Gemini "I wonder if I'm paying too much for internet service." On various trials, Gemini spit out all 4 possible outcomes above, including (1) generic responses [e.g., "If you haven't called them in 12 months, probably"]; (2) metadata summaries sometimes without personal data [e.g., "Gmail search shows a bill of $122 on September 4"] and sometimes with personal data [e.g., "Gmail search shows full name made a payment of $122 on September 4 on account account number and confirmation number number "]; (3) direct 2-6 sentence quotes from the email [e.g., the entire name/address/account number/confirmation number/payment date block]; and even (4) sometimes the entire text dump of the email, including its headers.

items.title: What's new in Node.js 27
items.content:
New Iterator superpower: zip, zipKeyed, join, and includes Pairing sequences lazily with Iterator.zip()

Combining endless iterators: solar generation and household consumption

Turning columns into objects with Iterator.zipKeyed()

Finishing pipelines with Iterator.prototype.join() and includes()

More accurate sums with Math.sumPrecise()

node:net/promises and async-iterable TCP servers

Virtual File System (node:vfs) is now unflagged

More Node.js Core upgrades: fs, Permissions, Test Runner, and HTTP Atomic temporary files with fs.mkstemp() and native fs.glob()

Built-in Test Runner: stable watch mode and Jest-style mock helpers

Why remove the prototype from req.headers?

Under the hood: V8 15.6, the 4 GB Heap Default, and OpenSSL 4.1

Heads-up: Node.js 27 breaking changes 1. req.headers has a null prototype

2. Memory limits for multi-process deployments

3. V8 serialization format and larger heap snapshots

4. V8 behavior changes that can break tests and caches

5. Deprecations, removals, and platform changes

Frequently Asked Questions Why did Node.js 27 start with an Alpha release in October 2026?

Will Node.js 27 become an LTS release even though 27 is an odd number?

What are the biggest JavaScript features in Node.js 27?

How did the default memory limit change in Node.js 27?

On October 29, 2026, the Node.js team published v27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0 . If you have been using Node.js for a few years, that version string alone probably made you do a double take. Where is the usual October v27.0.0 Current release?

Node.js 27 is the first release to follow the new annual schedule. Under the old schedule, October brought a major release that reached end of life six months later without entering Long Term Support (LTS). October now starts a six-month Alpha phase, ahead of the 27.0.0 Current release in April 2027 and LTS promotion in October 2027.

In this first Alpha, V8 moves from 14.6 to 15.6, adding Iterator.zip() , Iterator.zipKeyed() , Iterator.prototype.join() , Iterator.prototype.includes() , and Math.sumPrecise() . There is a promises API for node:net , along with async-iterable TCP servers. The Virtual File System ( node:vfs ) is now unflagged, the Permission Model gains --allow-env , and HTTP and memory defaults change too.

We’ll start with the JavaScript and Node.js APIs you can use in everyday code, comparing them with the older approaches. Then we’ll cover runtime changes and what to check before upgrading.

The main additions in Node.js 27 so far:

New Iterator helpers ( zip , zipKeyed , join , includes ) pair sequences, join their values into strings, and search them without collecting intermediate arrays.

Math.sumPrecise() sums an iterable of numbers without rounding each intermediate addition.

node:net/promises and async-iterable net.Server let you use async / await to set up TCP servers and sockets.

Virtual File System ( node:vfs ) is unflagged, making in-memory file systems and --vfs-load available without --experimental-vfs .

Core upgrades across fs , permissions, test runner, and http , including atomic temp files with fs.mkstemp() , --allow-env , Jest-style mock helpers, and a 65-second HTTP keepAliveTimeout .

V8 15.6 and OpenSSL 4.1 update sorting and cryptography, and the default heap limit rises to 4 GB on an 8 GB machine.

items.summary_ko: Node.js 27은 Iterator.zip, zipKeyed, join, includes와 Math.sumPrecise를 추가하며, node:net/promises, 가상 파일 시스템 node:vfs의 플래그 해제, 임시 파일용 fs.mkstemp와 네이티브 fs.glob 등을 포함한다. 주의할 점으로 req.headers가 null 프로토타입을 갖게 되는 호환성 변경과, V8 15.6, 기본 힙 4GB, OpenSSL 4.1 업그레이드가 있다.
items.content_ko: Node.js 27은 여러 새 기능을 소개한다. Iterator.zip()은 시퀀스를 지연 방식으로 짝지으며, zipKeyed()는 열을 객체로 바꾼다. Iterator.prototype.join()과 includes()로 파이프라인을 마무리할 수 있다. Math.sumPrecise()는 더 정확한 합계를 제공한다. node:net/promises와 비동기 반복 가능한 TCP 서버도 추가되었다. 가상 파일 시스템 node:vfs는 플래그 없이 사용할 수 있게 되었다. fs.mkstemp()로 임시 파일을 만들고 네이티브 fs.glob도 쓸 수 있다. 테스트 러너는 안정적인 watch 모드와 Jest 스타일 mock 도우미를 제공한다. 호환성 측면에서는 req.headers에 프로토타입이 없어지며, 다중 프로세스 배포의 메모리 제한, V8 직렬화 형식과 큰 힙 스냅샷, V8 동작 변경, 기타 deprecated 항목 등이 있다. 기반 구성요소는 V8 15.6, 기본 힙 4GB, OpenSSL 4.1이다. FAQ에 따르면 Node.js 27은 2026년 10월 알파로 시작했다.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Nvidia shares plunge as US tech giant investigates CEO Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
items.content:
Image source, CHRISTOPHE PETIT TESSON/POOL/EPA/Shutterstock

Image caption, Rubio is in Paris for a meeting of G7 foreign ministers

I’m travelling with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, at a G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, as he studiously avoids talking about the Jensen Huang story.

News of Huang’s statement and Nvidia’s investigation broke just before Rubio was motorcaded into a US airbase in Florida last night as we were about to get on the government plane.

On the tarmac we asked him about Huang but he wouldn’t address it, saying he couldn’t comment because of "the nature of it". Rubio’s involvement is key when it comes to questions about what the Trump administration knew when.

The New York Times reports that Rubio oversaw the drafting of a highly classified memo in the spring warning other top US officials that Huang was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.

The BBC has not independently verified the report and the State Department and the White House have not responded to our questions.

The timing matters because Huang remained a well-placed voice on AI policy with Trump, advocating looser export restrictions and selling all but the most up-to-date chips to China.

As we’ve reported, Huang accompanied Trump on his trip to Beijing in May, after the Rubio memo was circulated, according to the New York Times. I was part of the White House press pool on the trip, and saw Huang among other tech leaders including Elon Musk in the president’s close entourage.

The executives were brought into the heart of the world’s consequential bilateral relationship when Trump unexpectedly invited them into the room during one of the highly choreographed meetings with President Xi.

Nvidia, opening its investigation, says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

items.title: How ICE Keeps an Eye on Protestors
items.content:
While much of the florid, fashy antics of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE, has lingered long in the memory, there’s one thing the agency has been doing that’s largely flown under the radar—its efforts to surveil protesters using sophisticated tracking technologies. This represents a realization of warnings that privacy advocates have long expressed: the tools of the war on terror would be turned on Americans by an authoritarian. According to a recent report from Wired, during the unrest in Minneapolis last year, ICE utilized Reaper drones, Signal chat interceptions, financial tracking, license plate readers, and more to target activists.

The report focuses on how over 100 Homeland Security Investigations, or HSI, agents were deployed to infiltrate and monitor community meetings, marches, and general strikes in Minnesota. This was approved under a Trump directive from September of last year titled National Security Presidential Memorandum 7, issued after the assassination of Charlie Kirk. But this surveillance operation also relies on programs that date back to the early days of the PATRIOT Act.

This isn’t an isolated incident, either. Reporting suggests that ICE has been utilizing many of these surveillance tactics around the country, and there’s still much that is not known about these programs. Daniel Solove, a professor of intellectual property and technology law at George Washington University, tells The New Republic that he’s long expected these kinds of tools would eventually be used in the ways we are now seeing.

“The chickens have come home to roost,” Solove says. “We have an authoritarian government with all these surveillance technologies and minimal-to-no limits on what it can do with them. The legal controls are very weak, and now they’re abusing it. This isn’t a surprise. This is a disaster foretold.”

Solove says it’s still “outrageous” that it’s happening, but it’s not a shock to him. He says that warnings from privacy experts like himself have mostly “fallen on deaf ears among policymakers,” as they’ve chosen not to pass comprehensive privacy protections through Congress.

“This is exactly the type of scenario we’ve been warning about,” says Matthew Guariglia, a senior policy analyst at the Electronic Frontier Foundation. “The government has a very long history of surveilling people based on their political beliefs. In this new era, it’s not a surprise that the agency with carte blanche to buy and hoard as much surveillance equipment as possible, and that answers directly to the president, is the one being deployed to spy on protesters.”

Surveillance is “infrastructure,” Guariglia says, and whatever justification the government might give for buying all of these tools often isn’t the only thing they’ll use it for. They might argue it’s to fight crime or protect national security, but it can easily be turned against citizens practicing their First Amendment rights.

“At some point there’s going to need to be a huge accounting of what data DHS has collected in the last few years and what it’s been used for,” Guariglia says. “That includes data taken about protesters, any database that exists and how they’ve been using facial recognition. It also includes data they’ve been getting from other branches of government.”

The first Trump administration crossed a lot of lines and violated people’s rights, but it wasn’t known for deploying surveillance technologies at the scale we’re seeing today. The second Trump administration has far fewer guardrails and a clear focus on utilizing technology to help achieve its authoritarian aims.

“I don’t want to underplay the first Trump administration. There were terrible abuses,” Solove says. “But this one is different. It goes much, much further.”

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

제가 보기에는 블랙해커들 보다는 서버측이 클라이언트의 행동을 분석하는 과정처럼 보이더군요..

items.title: E-means: 10x faster k-means at equal loss
items.content:
100,000 datapoints in 200 clusters, two wide Gaussians and three small ones, cut off at a box, on a light uniform background. Lloyd has 1 update against 97 per epoch for e-means.

Across a large range of scales and datasets , e-means reaches a test loss below Lloyd's at 25 epochs, in 1.2 to 3 epochs. Measured end to end, that is a 10–45× wall-clock reduction on GPU against the state-of-the-art Lloyd implementation (Flash-KMeans [2] ), and 8–15× on CPU against Faiss [1] . Speed and quality usually trade against each other in k-means, while e-means achieves both better speed and loss.

Given a fixed dataset of n points X = {x 1 , ..., x n } ⊂ R d and an integer k , the k-means problem is to find k centroids C = (c 1 , ..., c k ) minimizing the mean squared distance between each point and its nearest centroid:

It's a static dataset, unlike codebook learning inside VQ-VAEs, where the distribution to cluster is constantly moving.

The goal of e-means is to provide a modern optimization rule for the k-means problem. We started this project from the following observations:

For e-means, we chose to do mini-batch updates with exponential moving averages [6] , which we found to be most efficient for the k-means problem. Contrary to previous mini-batch approaches, e-means requires no hyperparameter tuning because it automatically sets the batch size and step size with scaling laws (see Automatic hyperparameter tuning with scaling laws ). In addition, e-means improves the initialization and the dead-cluster revival strategy, adds a cosine-scheduled decay rate, and introduces a finalization stage that reduces the training loss for a negligible runtime penalty at the end of training. e-means is highly parallelizable, and comes with specialized kernels that translate its algorithmic advantage into wall-clock speedups.

Each mini-batch updates every cluster's count and sum. The centroid is their ratio.

Everything is derived from scaling laws.

Novel initialization and finalization methods. The run ends on each cluster's exact last-epoch mean.

The step α anneals from α 0 to 0.1 α 0 , as a learning rate does.

Clusters with size below a threshold are revived by splitting a large cluster.

GPU kernels fuse the nearest-centroid assignment, turning the epoch savings above into matching wall-clock speedups.

The centroid update rule is the central component of e-means. This section aims to provide an overview of update rules for k-means clustering. All methods maintain, for each cluster j , a sum S j and a count N j of the points assigned to it, and take the centroid as their ratio:

They differ only in how S j and N j are updated. Below, s j and n j denote the sum and the count of the points in the current batch that are assigned to cluster j (both zero if none are).

Lloyd’s algorithm [7] assigns every point to its nearest centroid and recomputes the statistics from scratch, using the full dataset as the batch:

so c j is the exact mean of the points currently assigned to it. Each update costs one full pass over the data, and the procedure is repeated a fixed number of times (typically 20 to 50 iterations).

MacQueen’s update [3] accumulates the statistics without ever discarding them:

so c j is the uniform mean of every point assigned to cluster j since the start of training, including points assigned under earlier, possibly poor, centroid positions. This was later partially addressed by Staleness-Reduction Mini-Batch K-Means [8] , a hybrid method between k-means and MacQueen. They obtained important speedups, but only on very low numbers of clusters.

e-means works on mini-batches and replaces this sum with an exponential moving average:

so older assignments are forgotten at rate α , and the centroid tracks recent assignments rather than the whole history. items.title_ko: 동일한 손실에서 10배 이상 빠른 k-means, e-means
items.summary_ko: e-means는 k-means 문제를 위한 최적화 규칙으로, 여러 규모와 데이터셋에서 25 에폭 동안 학습한 Lloyd 방식보다 낮은 테스트 손실에 1.2~3 에폭 만에 도달했다. 실제 실행 시간 기준으로 GPU에서는 최신 Lloyd 구현인 Flash-KMeans 대비 10~45배, CPU에서는 Faiss 대비 8~15배 빨라졌다고 보고했다. 일반적으로 k-means는 속도와 품질이 상충하지만, e-means는 속도와 손실 모두에서 개선을 보였다고 밝혔다.
items.content_ko: 본문은 10만 개의 데이터 포인트를 200개 클러스터로 나눈 예시로 시작한다. 이 데이터는 넓은 가우시안 분포 두 개와 작은 분포 세 개로 구성되며, 상자 영역으로 잘리고 밝은 균일 배경을 가진다. 에폭당 업데이트 횟수는 Lloyd가 1회, e-means가 97회다. 저자들은 다양한 규모와 데이터셋에서 e-means가 25 에폭 기준 Lloyd보다 낮은 테스트 손실에 1.2~3 에폭 만에 도달했다고 설명한다. 실행 시간을 측정한 결과 GPU에서는 Flash-KMeans [2] 대비 10~45배, CPU에서는 Faiss [1] 대비 8~15배 단축되었다. 본문은 k-means 문제를 정의하고, 정적 데이터셋을 다루는 이 연구가 분포가 계속 변하는 VQ-VAE 내부 코드북 학습과 다르다고 짚는다. e-means는 지수 이동 평균[6]을 활용한 미니배치 업데이트를 사용한다. 본문이 중간에 잘려 있다.

items.content:
Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 2: Yet another Instagram account-takeover trick is reportedly being abused, this time involving Meta’s AI chatbot. Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

New Instagram Unpatched Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title: Jensen Huang Admits Affair with Suspected Chinese Spy
items.content:
Jensen Huang has admitted to Nvidia’s board that he “had been intimate” with an executive U.S. officials accused of being a spy for the Chinese government. And the AI chip powerhouse said in a statement that it has opened an investigation into the matter. Previously, the New York Times reported that the U.S. government had alleged a woman named Alice Huang had been spying on Nvidia .

In an apology sent to company employees Sunday , Huang wrote, “I was unfaithful to my wife,” adding, “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Nvidia’s board released a statement confirming the investigation, writing that it will be overseen by “a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel,” and insisting that its board “prioritizes U.S. national and economic security” and “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.”

According to the board, Huang will continue to lead the company while the investigation is conducted.

The alleged spy, known by the names Alice Huang or Huang Le, was listed as Singapore-based Megaspeed’s managing director until at least 2023. The aim of the Nvidia operation, the Times wrote, was to learn more about Nvidia’s most advanced hardware. Chinese officials also allegedly tasked her with persuading Huang to lobby for shipping some of the company’s most advanced GPUs to China as a sort of stretch goal.

It’s unclear how much influence the alleged spy exerted or how successful she was. However, Jensen Huang did successfully petition Trump in 2025 to allow more GPU exports to China, and later struck a deal to also sell limited quantities of its second-most-powerful chip there.

Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives said in a email statement to Gizmodo that there “is clearly risk that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the Board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally.” Ives also predicts that this matter will only increase scrutiny regarding chips sales to China, which has remained a contentious issue in Washington.

items.title: Hate Chromium? Well, There’s a Linux Desktop Based on it Now
items.content:
Say the name " Chromium " out loud in Linux circles, and you will soon see what a mob looks like. Many people don't like how much of the web rests on one engine led by Google, and they prefer to keep it away from their systems.

Now we have Domicile, a new Rust-based Wayland compositor that uses a patched build of Chromium to draw the entire desktop as a web page.

Apps still run natively, and each Wayland window goes straight into Chromium's rendering system and shows up inside that page as an element. A window and a website can then sit side by side and be arranged the same way.

Some Domicile mockups as shown on the homepage.

Domicile is not a drop-in desktop like GNOME or KDE Plasma . It leaves the bar, the window layout, and the look to a shell , and that shell itself is a web page you have to write yourself.

Native app windows and websites both sit on that page, and because CSS decides where each one goes, layouts like tiling or floating take only a few lines of styling.

You can even swap the shell without closing a single window because loading a new one resets only the state held in the shell's own page. A single page can span every monitor, and shells are built from packages that anyone can publish on npm , whether it is a whole desktop, a bar, or a launcher.

The compositor still handles the lock screen, tray icons, notifications, and screen sharing, while the shell decides how they look. The built-in browser runs Manifest V3 Chrome extensions , but some of them behave differently than they do in Chrome.

Apps need Wayland support to run. Electron, SDL, and Qt apps start in Wayland mode, but X11-only ones will not run . Xwayland, the compatibility layer that lets X11 apps work on Wayland desktops, is something Domicile does not include.

The project is provided under the MIT license , and the Chromium files it modifies stick to Chromium's licenses. One more thing, and this could be a dealbreaker for some of you, the project is AI-assisted .

Not quite. Manganese is the ready-made shell that comes with Domicile, and it works as a complete tiling desktop out of the box. Its keybindings follow Sway 's on the Super key, and you get ten workspaces along with tabs, stacks, splits, floating windows, and a scratchpad.

Websites open as windows too, sitting next to native apps in the same layout, while extensions from the Chrome Web Store show up as buttons in the top bar.

It comes with a Settings app, clipboard history, launcher, screenshots tool, notifications, and a lock screen. Since every part of it is its own package, you can add a new item to the bar or replace the launcher while the rest stays as it is.

Packages exist for Fedora , openSUSE , Debian , Ubuntu , and Arch Linux , plus an AUR package for Arch users. For NixOS , or Nix on any distro, you can use the project's flake.

It runs only on x86_64 , and the project has no ARM builds.

A monolithic package carries Manganese, the login session, the domicile command, and the React packages that shells build against. After installing, you point a config file at the shell you want, then log out and pick " Domicile " on the login screen.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다
